data.name: Mata Hari
data.detailed_description:
NÃO CONFIES EM NINGUÉM SEM SER EM TI MESMO enquanto te aventuras no mundo sombrio da espionagem numa atmosfera instável de guerra iminente.
Como um agente duplo, terás de encontrar maneiras inteligentes de fazer as fações inimigas rivais lutar entre si enquanto iludes perseguidores em cada missão cada vez mais perigosa. Como uma mulher fatal, o teu charme notório consegue seduzir qualquer homem. Porém, será que o único homem que guarda a chave do teu coração será alguma vez teu?
Características
  • Baseado em eventos verídicos que levaram à 1ª Guerra Mundial
  • Desvende códigos, coloca telefones sobre escuta, usa a tua ingenuidade e usa os aparelhos mais recentes da era!
  • Arrisca tudo enquanto assumes missões perigosas
  • 8 mini-jogos desafiadores em 4 capítulos emocionantes
  • Uma variedade de finais diferentes dependendo das escolhas que fizeres durante o jogo

data.short_description: TRUST NO ONE BUT YOURSELF as you adventure into the dark world of espionage amidst the volatile atmosphere of impending war. As a double agent, you must find clever ways to pit enemy factions against each other while eluding pursuers in each of your increasingly dangerous missions.

reviews.review:
Mata Hari transforms the legendary dancer and suspected spy into the centerpiece of a traditional point-and-click adventure filled with political maneuvering, romance, espionage, and deception. Developed by 4Head Studios and published on Steam by Viva Media, the game draws inspiration from the turbulent period surrounding the famous historical figure without presenting itself as a strict recreation of her life. Instead, it embraces the mythology that grew around Mata Hari and constructs an international spy story in which charm, observation, intelligence gathering, and manipulation are essential tools for survival.

The historical European setting is one of the experience's strongest qualities. Taking place during an era of growing international tension, the story captures a world where elegant social gatherings and glamorous lifestyles coexist with secret intelligence operations and political instability. Mata Hari moves between these contrasting environments while becoming increasingly involved in dangerous assignments. This gives the narrative an appealing sense of duality: she can command attention as an exotic performer while simultaneously operating within a hidden world of agents, secrets, and competing national interests.

Gameplay remains firmly rooted in classic adventure-game traditions. Players explore locations, examine objects, gather useful information, engage characters in conversation, and solve problems that stand between Mata Hari and her objectives. This is not an action-heavy interpretation of espionage. Success generally comes from understanding situations and determining how information, objects, or relationships can be exploited. Players who enjoy carefully investigating environments will therefore get considerably more from the experience than those expecting frequent combat or fast-paced stealth sequences.

The espionage theme allows the puzzles to move beyond ordinary inventory manipulation. Mata Hari participates in intelligence-gathering activities involving period-appropriate techniques and technology, including code breaking and telephone tapping. These elements help reinforce the fantasy of operating as a spy during the early twentieth century, when surveillance required physical access, specialized equipment, personal connections, and considerable patience. The historical limitations of the technology actually benefit the adventure format because they naturally create opportunities for puzzles.

Several mini-games are distributed throughout the four-chapter story, with eight different activities intended to provide variety between conversations and exploration. These sequences represent different aspects of Mata Hari's unusual life and work, although their entertainment value is somewhat inconsistent. Some provide a pleasant change of pace, while others can feel like interruptions to the stronger investigative portions. They nevertheless demonstrate an effort to make the adventure more mechanically diverse than simply moving between locations and selecting dialogue options.

Mata Hari's career as a dancer also becomes part of the gameplay rather than serving merely as background information. This is important because it gives the protagonist an identity beyond being another fictional secret agent. Her public celebrity, personal relationships, romantic encounters, and clandestine activities intersect throughout the story. The game understands that her greatest weapon is often her ability to influence people rather than overpower them, making social interaction a natural component of its espionage fantasy.

Player decisions contribute to the outcome, and multiple endings provide some incentive to revisit the story or consider choices more carefully. The branching structure is relatively modest compared with contemporary narrative games, but it remains meaningful within a traditional adventure format. Mata Hari's loyalties, relationships, and actions can influence how events ultimately unfold, reinforcing the underlying themes of trust and betrayal. The possibility of different conclusions also suits a historical character whose actual activities remain surrounded by controversy and conflicting interpretations.

The visual presentation has naturally aged. Character models, facial expressions, and animations lack the fluidity expected from modern narrative adventures, and some interactions can appear rigid. However, the environments retain a degree of charm thanks to the period-inspired architecture, clothing, interiors, and European atmosphere. The game frequently feels like an illustrated espionage novel brought into interactive form, and that stylistic personality can compensate for some of its technical limitations.

Pacing will probably be the largest dividing point for modern players. Considerable time is spent talking, examining locations, collecting clues, and working through puzzles. Anyone accustomed to older PC adventures will recognize this rhythm immediately, but players expecting the excitement implied by the word "spy" may find the experience unexpectedly slow. Danger is primarily communicated through narrative circumstances rather than continuous action. Patience is therefore an important requirement.

Puzzle design can also show its age. Certain solutions require experimentation, and the intended path forward is not always immediately apparent. This occasionally results in frustration when progress depends on discovering a particular interaction rather than solving a clearly presented logical problem. At its best, however, the game rewards observation and deduction, especially when its puzzles incorporate espionage techniques instead of relying exclusively on arbitrary item combinations.

The writing and historical context ultimately carry much of the experience. The combination of romance, political tension, secret missions, dangerous acquaintances, and competing loyalties provides an appealing foundation for a spy adventure. While the characterization and dramatic presentation do not reach the standards of modern cinematic games, the unusual protagonist gives the narrative a personality that separates it from more conventional adventure stories.

Steam Deck users should approach Mata Hari as an older PC game without an official Steam Deck compatibility rating. It is neither officially Verified nor designated as a supported Deck release. Running it through Proton or using community configurations may produce different results depending on the setup, but players should not purchase it specifically for handheld use expecting guaranteed functionality.

Mata Hari is ultimately a niche but interesting adventure that benefits greatly from its protagonist and historical setting. Its aging technology, occasionally awkward puzzles, inconsistent mini-games, and leisurely pacing make it difficult to recommend universally, yet its combination of espionage, romance, dancing, code breaking, surveillance, conversation, and branching outcomes remains distinctive. For enthusiasts of classic point-and-click adventures who enjoy historical intrigue and are comfortable with older design conventions, it offers an unconventional journey through the glamorous and dangerous mythology surrounding one of espionage history's most recognizable figures.

Rating: 7/10
